title: Isolation
description: The isolation ladder a berth's process runs under, weakest first. A need names the weakest isolation it accepts (`Requirements.isolation`); an offer names the isolation it provides, and a task kind refuses an offer weaker than the need's (`Kind { label: "isolation" }`). placement-core's own copy of ark's ladder: ark-core maps `passport::EffectiveTier` onto it 1:1, and a berth offer's isolation is the weakest effective tier across its passport's processes (interfaces spec §D.2, §F, F6, F7). Ordered weakest to strongest (the Rust enum derives Ord); there is no `_ordinal` because it is not a reach. Source of truth: this schema; Rust mirror `placement_core::Isolation` (need.rs). TypeScript constants only: `_codegen` (no `rust` key, so codegen-rs writes nothing) and never `_dna`, so no constant reaches content_store_integrity and no DNA hash moves (interfaces spec §2.G, G11). placement-core's schema_contract test reads this file with include_str! and compares it, in order, with the variants of `placement_core::Isolation` written out by hand inside that test. It catches a value changed here, but a variant added to the Rust enum without editing the test still passes: nothing ties the test's list to the enum (follow-on: an `ALL` const in need.rs held to the enum by an exhaustive match, read by the test).
